verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II is scheduled to launch Wednesday, April 1'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is set to launch on April 1, 2026'; R4: 'slated to launch as early as April 1'; R5: 'on April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the scheduled launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II has a targeted lift-off time of 6:24 PM EDT (2224 GMT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'two-hour window starting at 6:24 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'opening of today’s launch window is slated for just over 4 hours from now, at 6:24 p.m. EDT'; R3: '5:24 pm CT' (equivalent to 6:24 PM EDT)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm the targeted liftoff time as 6:24 PM EDT.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch from Launch Complex 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center'; R2: 'Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R5: 'from Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day journey around the moon'; R2: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R4: 'lasting about 10 days'; R5: '10-day journey'; R7: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent description across sources as a 10-day mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission's four-astronaut crew'; R2: 'four astronauts'; R3: 'Four astronauts'; R4: 'send four astronauts around the moon'; R5: '4 astronauts'; R7: 'four-member crew around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on a lunar flyby/orbit mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar flight since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'For the first time since 1972'; R4: 'first flight to the moon since 1972'; R5: 'first time in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first crewed lunar mission since 1972 (Apollo 17).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch window is open until 7:24 PM CT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the window is 5:24–7:24 pm CT'; R1: 'two-hour window starting at 6:24 p.m. EDT' (ends 8:24 PM EDT = 7:24 PM CT)
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states window until 7:24 PM CT; R1 equivalent in EDT.

verifications.claim: The mission goal of Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; 'test flight'; R2: 'test flight'; R4: 'test flight, lasting about 10 days, will send four astronauts around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it precisely as a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in R2, R3, R4, R5, R7
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed consistently across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: If Artemis II is delayed, subsequent launch windows are available starting April 2, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'If the mission cannot launch on April 1, the next available launch window dates... April 2: 6:22 pm CDT'
verifications.reasoning: R3 explicitly lists subsequent windows starting April 2, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis I was an uncrewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uncrewed Orion spacecraft... Artemis I'; R3: 'Artemis I, was an uncrewed test mission'; R6: 'uncrewed Moon-orbiting mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis I as uncrewed.

verifications.claim: Artemis I successfully launched on November 16, 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I rocket launching... 16 November 2022'; R6: 'Launch date November 16, 2022'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date and successful launch confirmed.
